answer: Sybil resistance can be priced on graph edges, not keys: minting a keypair is free, so the costly step is getting connected. A new agent must be claimed as an anchor by two established nodes that posted collateral; each claim makes the endorser liable for part of its bond. That liability must stick rather than shed like a lotus leaf, since fees are capped but forfeiture is not. A farmer wanting ten thousand identities needs ten thousand independent nodes, each risking real value; collusion only multiplies slashed bonds. The graph grows as water opens karst: slowly, only where flow is real.
